title: Michael D: v1 feeders - shared harness, host calendar-read/gmail-triage/tasks-classifier, GHA todoist-brief, host task registrar, seat recorder and metering
executive_summary: Child D gives Michael the v1 model-free feeders: a shared harness (ET window, per-date dedupe, ordering), three host feeders on the chairman grant, todoist-brief on GHA, the host task registrar, and the seat-side recorder that closes the classify queue and writes metering.

functional_requirements.description: feeder.mjs exports runFeeder({ feeder, venue, window, upstream, run }, { sb, env, now, logger }) in the michael-family shape (VALIDATION c26274e9 condition 3: every feeder is `export async function runX({ sb, argv, now, ...deps })` plus a private main(); no exported main(argv, deps)). The harness: (a) moves hhmmToMinutes/inWindow out of scripts/michael-quiet-tick.mjs:35-46 into feeder.mjs and re-imports them in the tick (no third copy); (b) is inert outside [window.start, window.end) ET with { ok:true, action:'inert', reason:'outside_et_window' } and exit 0; (c) pre-flights michael_feeder_runs via readRows and returns { ok:true, action:'inert', reason:'tables_absent' } while the child B migration is unapplied (never a throw, never a write); (d) single-flight: a row for (feeder, et_date) with status running-equivalent (started_at set, finished_at null, started_at younger than 10 minutes) makes the fire inert with reason 'in_flight'; an existing ok row makes it inert with reason 'already_ok' (a degraded or failed row allows a retry); (e) attempt = max(attempt)+1 with one retry on the unique-index conflict (23505) before returning failed; (f) upstream: [{ feeder, accept:['ok','degraded'] }] checked against today's rows, unmet yields inert reason 'upstream_not_ready'; (g) writes the run row on start (started_at) and completion (finished_at, status ok|degraded|failed|skipped, counts, log_md of counts and ids only) with model_used/tokens_in/tokens_out null for task_scheduler and gha venues; (h) maps a coded throw from getAuthenticatedClient (HOST_VENUE_REQUIRED, MICHAEL_ENCRYPTION_KEY_MISSING, NO_STORED_TOKENS, invalid_grant) to status failed with counts.error_code; (i) PII-safe single-line JSON logs `[michael:<feeder>] {...}` with counts and ids only; (j) gracefulExit for the Task Scheduler venue. It also exports the pure assembleReadiness({ runs, now }) predicate of spec section 5 line 109 for child E: wait until calendar ok and gmail/todoist ok-or-degraded, proceed degraded at or after 05:45 ET with headsUp naming the missing feeders. rules-match.mjs exports matchGmailRule(rule_json, thread) (from/subject/list-id/label predicates, case-insensitive, all-of semantics), matchKeywordBuckets(rule_json, text) for the tasks four-bucket routing, and roleTagFor(rules, task) for todoist; each pure, each returning { matched, rule_key } or null. PLAN amendments (DESIGN F1-F9, F18, F20; DATABASE DB-D3; SECURITY F-9; TESTING D-1, D-2, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7): (a) inWindow keeps its INCLUSIVE [start, end] semantics when it moves to feeder.mjs (both the tick and the feeders use it; FR-1(b) is restated inclusive so every host feeder keeps its last :00/:30 retry) and the window parameter becomes required, the tick passing WINDOW_ET explicitly at its two call sites; export etMinuteOfDay(now) and use it in the tick. (b) The config object gains etDateOverride; every feeder parses --et-date (never --date) per family convention and passes it down; --date is unsupported on feeders. (c) Exit codes are three-way: 0 for inert, ok and degraded; 1 when a status failed run row was written; 2 for a refusal with no row and no work (coded throws, bad args, MODIFY_NOT_LANDED, wrong venue). (d) logger defaults to a stderr writer; under --json stdout contains exactly one parseable JSON object. (e) gracefulExit(exitCode, { backstopMs }) is defined once in feeder.mjs, never imported from a cron script. (f) A frozen FEEDERS registry (calendar-read, gmail-triage, tasks-classifier, todoist-brief, seat-classify, retention) is exported; runFeeder refuses an unregistered id with FEEDER_UNKNOWN. (g) assembleReadiness({ runs, now, required = READINESS_REQUIREMENTS, deadlineEt = BRIEF_DEADLINE_ET }) with both constants exported; the tick imports BRIEF_DEADLINE_ET in the same edit. (h) The start row is written status skipped with counts { phase: started } (there is no running value in the CHECK and failed would inflate the chairman-facing QUIET_TICK_FEEDER_FAILED gauge); the finish write sets the real terminal status. (i) Attempt allocation is INSERT (never upsert) on et_date,feeder,attempt with attempt = max+1 from one bounded read; lib/michael/db.mjs writeRows gains code and details passthrough on both WRITE_FAILED branches (additive, no caller reads them today) and feeder.mjs exports isUniqueViolation(res) matching code 23505 or /duplicate key value|already exists/i; losing the race twice is inert reason in_flight, never failed. (j) The in-flight staleness threshold is a per-feeder constant at or above the fire interval (20 minutes for */15 feeders), the fence compared as an ISO string, never a Date. (k) The tables_absent inert envelope also sets tables_absent: true. (l) The quiet-tick regression floor is its measured 11 tests / 26 assertions (not 62).

functional_requirements.description: runCalendarRead({ sb, argv, now, auth, calendar }) under runFeeder (feeder 'calendar-read', venue task_scheduler, window 04:00-05:00 ET, no upstream): events.list today plus or minus one ET day on 'primary' and MICHAEL_EXELON_CALENDAR_ID; upserts michael_calendar_day by (et_date, event_id) for the three dates with calendar_id, title, starts_at, ends_at, all_day, response_status, coded_marker (a leading bracket tag such as [DEEP] or [OFFICE] parsed from the title), optional (needsAction or tentative response, or 'optional' in the title), overlap_group (events on the same date whose intervals intersect share a group id); day classification for today (Recovery when no non-optional events, Interpersonal when three or more accepted meetings, Deep when a coded [DEEP] event exists or fewer than two meetings, Shallow otherwise; coded-event override wins; Tuesday-office rule marks Tuesday Interpersonal when any accepted in-office event exists) written into the run row counts as { classification, events_by_date, coded, optional, overlaps }. Any calendar API failure marks the run failed; a single calendar failing marks degraded and records which. PLAN amendments (DATABASE DB-D7; SECURITY F-11; DESIGN F5): calendar-read calls assertHostVenue(env) at the top of runCalendarRead before any client resolution and regardless of injected auth, mapping the coded throw to a refusal. Events carrying the same event_id on both calendars are deduped in memory before the upsert, preferring primary, and counts.cross_calendar_collisions records the number. Rows are written only under --apply (dry-run is the default and prints what would be written).

functional_requirements.description: runGmailTriage({ sb, argv, now, auth, gmail }) under runFeeder (feeder 'gmail-triage', venue task_scheduler, window 04:30-05:30 ET, no upstream): labels.list reconciles michael_gmail_labels (upsert by label_id with name and last_seen_in_gmail_at; a configured label missing from Gmail marks the run degraded, records counts.missing_labels and skips that class); threads.list for `in:inbox newer_than:1d` minus every keep_in_inbox label plus the older-than-1d sweep `in:inbox older_than:1d`, bounded by maxResults 200 per query; getThreadMeta per thread (metadata only); rules-first matching against active michael_rules domain gmail through matchGmailRule; matched threads are written to michael_gmail_triage_items by (et_date, thread_id) with class, rule_key, last_message_id and action_intent derived from the rule (label id, archive) but NO threads.modify call in this PR (--dry-run is the only mode; --apply is refused with APPLY_NOT_LANDED until PR 4b); unmatched threads are written with class null (queued for the seat); fleet-class threads (rule class 'fleet') are written class 'fleet' and left for the seat and child G (no handoff written). PLAN amendments (SECURITY F-2, F-11; DATABASE DB-D4, DB-D5, DB-D13; DESIGN F11; TESTING G-6): action_intent is derived only from a matching active rule with auto_apply true AND auto_apply_verb in (label, archive), mirroring FR-7; a matching rule with auto_apply false still writes class and rule_key with action_intent null. Item writes are two-step: upsert with ignoreDuplicates true on et_date,thread_id (create-if-absent), then update class, rule_key, action_intent, last_message_id filtered by .is(action_taken_at, null) so the guard is a server-side predicate; every batch row carries an identical key set and never a column the feeder does not own (action_taken_at, verified_by, needs_you, summary). The label reconcile writes only label_id, name and last_seen_in_gmail_at, never class, keep_in_inbox or summarize; the configured set is seeded by child F (Cowork import, spec line 143) and until then the keep_in_inbox exclusion is a documented no-op. The acted-row guard read is narrowed to the batch thread ids rather than the whole day. assertHostVenue(env) runs at the top of runGmailTriage regardless of injected auth. Bodies are never fetched (TS-5 asserts format metadata).

functional_requirements.description: Adds --apply: for each item row with action_intent and no action_taken_at, in creation order, call modifyThread (lib/michael/gmail-client.mjs, TRASH/SPAM already refused) then set action_taken_at; count counts.threads_modified; when the count would exceed MICHAEL_GMAIL_MODIFY_CEILING (default 60) stop applying, mark the run degraded with counts.ceiling_hit=true, and leave the remaining intents for the next run or the seat; a thread previously archived (an earlier row with action_intent archive and action_taken_at set) that reappears in the inbox with a newer last_message_id is written borderline=true with class kept and no automatic action; a modify failure records the item as failed in counts.modify_failed and continues; the run is failed only when every modify failed or the API is unreachable. The re-run rule: a killed run re-executed acts only on intents without action_taken_at (record-then-act, spec section 5 and 11 idempotency test). PLAN amendments (SECURITY F-1, F-3, F-9; RISK condition 1, S3; DESIGN F5): the Gmail-mutating half is behind a distinct --modify flag (never --apply, which for every feeder means write rows): --apply without --modify records intents and writes rows only; --modify executes intents. Before PR 4b lands, --modify is refused MODIFY_NOT_LANDED. The ceiling is a per-ET-date budget: the harness sums counts.threads_modified across every prior gmail-triage run for the date (the same bounded read single-flight uses), and once the date total reaches MICHAEL_GMAIL_MODIFY_CEILING the run writes counts.ceiling_hit true and every later fire that day is inert with reason ceiling_hit until a human clears it; degraded re-arms a retry EXCEPT when the degradation reason is the ceiling. The registrar registers gmail-triage WITHOUT --modify (shadow phase); promotion is an explicit chairman re-register (--remove then register --with-modify) after one full dry-run morning. Bulk or by-run unarchive is out of scope for D and recorded as a residual for a later child.

functional_requirements.description: runTasksClassifier({ sb, argv, now, auth, drive, todoist }) under runFeeder (feeder 'tasks-classifier', venue task_scheduler, window 03:45-04:30 ET, no upstream): reads current-tasks.json from MICHAEL_TASKS_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID through readDriveFileText; aborts skipped with counts.reason stale when the file's modifiedTime is older than 36 hours, and skipped with reason cleanup_pending when a cleanup-pending.json exists in the folder that is newer than the last consumed marker (recorded in counts of the last ok run); routes each item by matchKeywordBuckets against active michael_rules domain tasks into the four buckets (rule_json names the bucket and target Todoist project/label); items no rule routes are staged to michael_staged_items kind 'task_route' for the seat's grading; dedupes against Todoist by fetching tasks with labels captured and from-google-tasks created in the last 7 days and comparing normalized content; creates tasks through the injected Todoist client with both labels; writes the consumed set as cleanup-pending content back to Drive only when the grant carries drive.file write (it does not in v1: drive.readonly), so v1 STAGES the cleanup list to michael_staged_items kind 'tasks_cleanup' with the file ids and records counts.cleanup_staged; the Apps Script consumer is out of scope. PLAN amendments (RISK condition 3, DA1; SECURITY F-7, F-11; DATABASE DB-D6; DESIGN F10): assertHostVenue(env) runs at the top of runTasksClassifier. Staged payloads are bounded and explicitly keyed: task_route rows carry { dedupe_key: <et_date>:<source item id>, dedupe_sha256, title: first 200 chars, source_file_id, reason } and tasks_cleanup rows carry { dedupe_key, dedupe_sha256, item_ids, count }; never a Drive file body or an email address. Before inserting, open rows of that kind are read through the partial index (.eq(kind).is(dispositioned_at, null), bounded) and only unseen dedupe_keys are inserted. Because michael_staged_items is on retention NEVER_TOUCHED, scripts/michael/retention.mjs is extended (code, no DDL) to null the payload of DISPOSITIONED staged rows older than 30 days, keeping kind, disposition and timestamps; TR-4 records that undispositioned rows persist until dispositioned. Rows are written and Todoist tasks created only under --apply.
acceptance_criteria: tasks-classifier.test.js: stale file yields skipped/stale with no Todoist call; unconsumed cleanup yields skipped/cleanup_pending; four-bucket routing from rule fixtures; unrouted items staged; dedupe against a seeded recent task creates nothing; created tasks carry both labels; the cleanup list is staged, never written to Drive in v1

functional_requirements.description: runTodoistBrief({ sb, argv, now, todoist }) under runFeeder (feeder 'todoist-brief', venue gha, window 04:45-05:30 ET, no upstream): fetches all tasks through the injected client (createTodoistClient at the private main), filters due today or overdue in ET, excludes projects named EVA and For Processing (by name from getProjects) and the EHG chairman project id (read only to count the EHG pointer into counts.ehg_pointer); role_tag from a rules row domain todoist via roleTagFor; items with an `Est:` line in content or description get effort_grade deterministically (S under 30 minutes, M under 90, L otherwise) and est_minutes; the rest keep effort_grade null (queued for the seat); upserts michael_todoist_snapshot by (et_date, task_id) never overwriting a row whose chosen_action or moved_back_at is set; overnight mutations only for active michael_rules with auto_apply=true and auto_apply_verb in label/reschedule (label updates; keep MICHAEL_DAILY_CHECKIN_TASK_ID due today), each deduped on (et_date, task_id, action) inside mutations_applied and redacted to content_sha256 like todoist-act.mjs; every other date change waits for the conversation. Workflow .github/workflows/michael-todoist-brief-cron.yml: name, two cron lines ('*/15 8-9 * * *' EDT and '*/15 9-10 * * *' EST with the ET window in a trailing comment), workflow_dispatch, permissions contents read, concurrency group ${{ github.workflow }} cancel-in-progress true, timeout-minutes 10, node 22 with npm cache, npm ci --ignore-scripts, env SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, TODOIST_API_TOKEN, run `node scripts/michael/todoist-brief.mjs --apply` with no cd. tests/unit/cron/michael-todoist-brief-wiring.test.js forks michael-retention-wiring.test.js allowing exactly TODOIST_API_TOKEN in addition. PLAN amendments (DESIGN F16; TESTING 4.10; DATABASE DB-D4): the cron pair with trailing ET comment is copied from chairman-morning-brief-cron.yml lines 29-30 (retention supplies the secrets, env and steps skeleton). The env key order in the workflow is SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, TODOIST_API_TOKEN (last), and the wiring test at tests/unit/cron/michael-todoist-brief-wiring.test.js drops TODOIST from the forked negative regex while keeping the positive exact-set assertion. Snapshot writes use the guarded shape: create-if-absent with ignoreDuplicates, then update filtered by .is(chosen_action, null).is(moved_back_at, null); rows never carry chosen_action, mutations_applied or moved_back_at from the feeder. mutations_applied is appended as an array.
acceptance_criteria: todoist-brief.test.js: exclusion by project name and id; Est parsing and grading; ungraded rows null; role tags; auto_apply label/reschedule applied once and deduped on re-run; a row with chosen_action set is not overwritten; the check-in task is kept due today

functional_requirements.description: In the scripts/setup-alarm-cron-tasks.mjs shape: MICHAEL_HOST_TASKS = [tasks-classifier 03:45-04:30, calendar-read 04:00-05:00, gmail-triage 04:30-05:30] each { taskName 'EHG Michael <feeder>' (no colon, QF-20260906-961), script 'scripts/michael/<feeder>.mjs --apply', wrapperRelPath 'scripts/cron/michael-<feeder>-task.cmd', intervalMinutes 15, startTime '00:00' }; the in-script window makes off-window fires inert. Pure builders reused or mirrored: buildWrapperScript (CRLF, `cd /d <repo root>`, `call node <script>`), buildHiddenTrAction (quoted wscript.exe //B run-hidden.vbs wrapper), buildCreateArgs adding /RU <current user> and /NP as in setup-eva-watcher-task.mjs:97-108 so a fire never opens a console, buildRemoveArgs, buildQueryArgs, buildQueryXmlArgs, verifyHiddenLaunch on the OS-returned XML; CLI register (default) | --dry-run | --status | --verify | --remove; refuses to register when run-hidden.vbs is absent; win32 guard exits 2 elsewhere. Wake-from-sleep is not configured (the /XML import path is denied unelevated on this host) and the header states the laptop must be awake; a missed window is a failed run visible to the gauge. VALIDATION condition 6: before committing, measure from PowerShell that an unelevated `schtasks /Create /SC MINUTE /MO 15 /ST 00:00 /F` of a throwaway task succeeds on this host and record the transcript line in the PR body; if it is denied, the registrar documents the elevated one-time step instead of claiming unelevated works. PLAN amendments (RISK condition 2, T1, O1; DESIGN F13, F14, F15, F17; SECURITY F-16; TESTING G-4): the VALIDATION-condition-6 measurement is done (RISK e1639df4, PowerShell, unelevated, this host): plain /Create /SC MINUTE /MO 15 /ST 00:00 /F succeeds at LogonType InteractiveToken; adding /RU <user> /NP prompts for a password and is denied. Therefore the registrar does NOT pass /RU or /NP and reuses the alarm builders by name (buildWrapperScript, buildHiddenTrAction, buildCreateArgs, buildRemoveArgs, buildQueryArgs, buildQueryXmlArgs, verifyHiddenLaunch from scripts/setup-alarm-cron-tasks.mjs; never its parseArgs or main), relying on run-hidden.vbs for console suppression exactly as all ten existing EHG host tasks do. Task names are validated against the imported TASK_NAME_ILLEGAL_CHARS inside the build path (QF-20260906-961). The registrar exports main(argv, deps) returning { exitCode, action } like its setup-* siblings (TR-1 private-main rule applies to michael verbs, not to the registrar). Wrappers under scripts/cron/michael-<feeder>-task.cmd are generated at register time and gitignored, never committed. The header states both preconditions: the host must be awake (no wake configured) and on mains power (the sibling tasks carry DisallowStartIfOnBatteries). Merge order: this PR lands after PR 4b. The registered gmail-triage command carries --apply but not --modify.

THE THROUGH-LINE. The harness is the right idea and the two-argument runFeeder(payload, deps) shape is CORRECT - it matches lib/michael/gmail-client.mjs:26 modifyThread(payload, deps), and TR-1's one-argument rule governs runX VERBS, not library functions. F1 IS THE ONE WITH A MEASURED COST. FR-1(a) says re-import the tick's window predicate with no third copy; FR-1(b) says half-open. The predicate at michael-quiet-tick.mjs:45 is inclusive. # Product Requirements Document

## Strategic Directive
SD-LEO-ORCH-MICHAEL-ROLE-FORMALIZATION-002-D

## Title
Michael D: v1 feeders - shared harness, host calendar-read/gmail-triage/tasks-classifier, GHA todoist-brief, host task registrar, seat recorder and metering

## Status
Planning

## Executive Summary
Child D gives Michael the v1 model-free feeders: a shared harness (ET window, per-date dedupe, ordering), three host feeders on the chairman grant, todoist-brief on GHA, the host task registrar, and the seat-side recorder that closes the classify queue and writes metering.

## Functional Requirements
### FR-1: Shared feeder harness lib/michael/feeder.mjs and pure rules matcher lib/michael/rules-match.mjs (PR 1)
feeder.mjs exports runFeeder({ feeder, venue, window, upstream, run }, { sb, env, now, logger }) in the michael-family shape (VALIDATION c26274e9 condition 3: every feeder is `export async function runX({ sb, argv, now, ...deps })` plus a private main(); no exported main(argv, deps)). The harness: (a) moves hhmmToMinutes/inWindow out of scripts/michael-quiet-tick.mjs:35-46 into feeder.mjs and re-imports them in the tick (no third copy); (b) is inert outside [window.start, window.end) ET with { ok:true, action:'inert', reason:'outside_et_window' } and exit 0; (c) pre-flights michael_feeder_runs via readRows and returns { ok:true, action:'inert', reason:'tables_absent' } while the child B migration is unapplied (never a throw, never a write); (d) single-flight: a row for (feeder, et_date) with status running-equivalent (started_at set, finished_at null, started_at younger than 10 minutes) makes the fire inert with reason 'in_flight'; an existing ok row makes it inert with reason 'already_ok' (a degraded or failed row allows a retry); (e) attempt = max(attempt)+1 with one retry on the unique-index conflict (23505) before returning failed; (f) upstream: [{ feeder, accept:['ok','degraded'] }] checked against today's rows, unmet yields inert reason 'upstream_not_ready'; (g) writes the run row on start (started_at) and completion (finished_at, status ok|degraded|failed|skipped, counts, log_md of counts and ids only) with model_used/tokens_in/tokens_out null for task_scheduler and gha venues; (h) maps a coded throw from getAuthenticatedClient (HOST_VENUE_REQUIRED, MICHAEL_ENCRYPTION_KEY_MISSING, NO_STORED_TOKENS, invalid_grant) to status failed with counts.error_code; (i) PII-safe single-line JSON logs `[michael:<feeder>] {...}` with counts and ids only; (j) gracefulExit for the Task Scheduler venue. It also exports the pure assembleReadiness({ runs, now }) predicate of spec section 5 line 109 for child E: wait until calendar ok and gmail/todoist ok-or-degraded, proceed degraded at or after 05:45 ET with headsUp naming the missing feeders. rules-match.mjs exports matchGmailRule(rule_json, thread) (from/subject/list-id/label predicates, case-insensitive, all-of semantics), matchKeywordBuckets(rule_json, text) for the tasks four-bucket routing, and roleTagFor(rules, task) for todoist; each pure, each returning { matched, rule_key } or null.

Acceptance:
- lib/michael/feeder.test.js pins: inert outside window; inert tables_absent with zero writes; in_flight and already_ok single-flight; attempt max+1 and the 23505 retry; upstream_not_ready; counts-only log corpus (a test asserts no '@' and no thread subject text appears in captured log lines); coded-throw to failed mapping; assembleReadiness wait/proceed-degraded/proceed cases
- scripts/michael-quiet-tick.mjs imports hhmmToMinutes/inWindow from lib/michael/feeder.mjs and its 62 existing tests stay green
- lib/michael/rules-match.test.js pins gmail predicates, keyword buckets and role tags on rule_json fixtures

### FR-2: Google API legs on the chairman grant: lib/michael/google-clients.mjs and env-resolved constants (PR 2)
google-clients.mjs exports listCalendarEvents({ calendarId, timeMin, timeMax }, { auth, calendarFactory }) over calendar.events.list (singleEvents, orderBy startTime, maxResults 250), listDriveFiles({ folderId, name }, { auth, driveFactory }) and readDriveFileText({ fileId }, { auth, driveFactory }) over drive.files.list/get(alt=media) with drive.readonly, and extends lib/michael/gmail-client.mjs with listThreads({ q, maxResults }, deps), getThreadMeta({ threadId }, deps) (metadata format only: From, Subject, List-Id, labelIds, last message id; never a body) and listLabels(deps). Every function is import-time pure, lazy-imports googleapis in a default factory, takes an injected auth or resolves one through getAuthenticatedClient({ sb, enc, env }), never throws (returns { ok:false, error }), and never logs a token. lib/michael/constants.mjs resolves chairman constants from env with named refusals when absent: MICHAEL_EXELON_CALENDAR_ID, MICHAEL_TASKS_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID, MICHAEL_EHG_CHAIRMAN_PROJECT_ID (default 6grHWpvVM8QXrj5W per lib/integrations/todoist/chairman-notify.js:25), MICHAEL_DAILY_CHECKIN_TASK_ID, MICHAEL_GMAIL_MODIFY_CEILING (default 60). No chairman identifier is hard-coded in a feeder.

Acceptance:
- lib/michael/google-clients.test.js: each client maps its call arguments exactly (calendarId/timeMin/timeMax/singleEvents; q/maxResults; fileId alt media), returns { ok:false, error } on a rejecting factory, and importing with no env does not throw
- gmail-client.test.js extended: getThreadMeta requests format metadata with the four headers only and never a full body
- constants.test.js: missing MICHAEL_EXELON_CALENDAR_ID yields refusal CONSTANT_MISSING naming the variable; the ceiling default is 60 and parses an env override

### FR-3: scripts/michael/calendar-read.mjs on the host (PR 3)
runCalendarRead({ sb, argv, now, auth, calendar }) under runFeeder (feeder 'calendar-read', venue task_scheduler, window 04:00-05:00 ET, no upstream): events.list today plus or minus one ET day on 'primary' and MICHAEL_EXELON_CALENDAR_ID; upserts michael_calendar_day by (et_date, event_id) for the three dates with calendar_id, title, starts_at, ends_at, all_day, response_status, coded_marker (a leading bracket tag such as [DEEP] or [OFFICE] parsed from the title), optional (needsAction or tentative response, or 'optional' in the title), overlap_group (events on the same date whose intervals intersect share a group id); day classification for today (Recovery when no non-optional events, Interpersonal when three or more accepted meetings, Deep when a coded [DEEP] event exists or fewer than two meetings, Shallow otherwise; coded-event override wins; Tuesday-office rule marks Tuesday Interpersonal when any accepted in-office event exists) written into the run row counts as { classification, events_by_date, coded, optional, overlaps }. Any calendar API failure marks the run failed; a single calendar failing marks degraded and records which.

Acceptance:
- calendar-read.test.js: fixture events across the three dates yield the expected upsert rows and natural key, coded_marker parsing, optional flags, overlap groups, and each classification branch including the Tuesday-office rule and the coded override
- One calendar rejecting yields status degraded with counts.failed_calendar; both rejecting yields failed; GITHUB_ACTIONS=true yields failed with error_code HOST_VENUE_REQUIRED and no API call
- Outside 04:00-05:00 ET the script exits 0 inert with no API call

### FR-4: scripts/michael/gmail-triage.mjs part 1: label reconcile and rules-first matching, read-only (PR 4a)
runGmailTriage({ sb, argv, now, auth, gmail }) under runFeeder (feeder 'gmail-triage', venue task_scheduler, window 04:30-05:30 ET, no upstream): labels.list reconciles michael_gmail_labels (upsert by label_id with name and last_seen_in_gmail_at; a configured label missing from Gmail marks the run degraded, records counts.missing_labels and skips that class); threads.list for `in:inbox newer_than:1d` minus every keep_in_inbox label plus the older-than-1d sweep `in:inbox older_than:1d`, bounded by maxResults 200 per query; getThreadMeta per thread (metadata only); rules-first matching against active michael_rules domain gmail through matchGmailRule; matched threads are written to michael_gmail_triage_items by (et_date, thread_id) with class, rule_key, last_message_id and action_intent derived from the rule (label id, archive) but NO threads.modify call in this PR (--dry-run is the only mode; --apply is refused with APPLY_NOT_LANDED until PR 4b); unmatched threads are written with class null (queued for the seat); fleet-class threads (rule class 'fleet') are written class 'fleet' and left for the seat and child G (no handoff written).

Acceptance:
- gmail-triage.test.js part 1: a missing configured label degrades and skips only that class; keep_in_inbox labels are excluded from the query; matched threads carry rule_key and action_intent; unmatched threads are class null; no modify call exists in the module (source assertion); bodies are never requested (format metadata asserted)
- Idempotent: re-running with the same fixture writes no duplicate rows (upsert on the natural key) and does not overwrite a row whose action_taken_at is set

### FR-5: gmail-triage part 2: record-then-act with the modify ceiling and borderline resurfacing (PR 4b)
Adds --apply: for each item row with action_intent and no action_taken_at, in creation order, call modifyThread (lib/michael/gmail-client.mjs, TRASH/SPAM already refused) then set action_taken_at; count counts.threads_modified; when the count would exceed MICHAEL_GMAIL_MODIFY_CEILING (default 60) stop applying, mark the run degraded with counts.ceiling_hit=true, and leave the remaining intents for the next run or the seat; a thread previously archived (an earlier row with action_intent archive and action_taken_at set) that reappears in the inbox with a newer last_message_id is written borderline=true with class kept and no automatic action; a modify failure records the item as failed in counts.modify_failed and continues; the run is failed only when every modify failed or the API is unreachable. The re-run rule: a killed run re-executed acts only on intents without action_taken_at (record-then-act, spec section 5 and 11 idempotency test).

Acceptance:
- 80 seeded matched threads with ceiling 60 yield exactly 60 modifyThread calls, status degraded and ceiling_hit=true; the remaining 20 rows keep action_intent with no action_taken_at
- A run interrupted after 30 modifies and re-run makes exactly the remaining modify calls and none of the first 30 (idempotency)
- A previously archived thread with a newer last_message_id is written borderline=true and not modified
- A modify rejecting for one thread leaves that row without action_taken_at, counts.modify_failed=1, and the run continues

### FR-6: scripts/michael/tasks-classifier.mjs on the host (PR 5)
runTasksClassifier({ sb, argv, now, auth, drive, todoist }) under runFeeder (feeder 'tasks-classifier', venue task_scheduler, window 03:45-04:30 ET, no upstream): reads current-tasks.json from MICHAEL_TASKS_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID through readDriveFileText; aborts skipped with counts.reason stale when the file's modifiedTime is older than 36 hours, and skipped with reason cleanup_pending when a cleanup-pending.json exists in the folder that is newer than the last consumed marker (recorded in counts of the last ok run); routes each item by matchKeywordBuckets against active michael_rules domain tasks into the four buckets (rule_json names the bucket and target Todoist project/label); items no rule routes are staged to michael_staged_items kind 'task_route' for the seat's grading; dedupes against Todoist by fetching tasks with labels captured and from-google-tasks created in the last 7 days and comparing normalized content; creates tasks through the injected Todoist client with both labels; writes the consumed set as cleanup-pending content back to Drive only when the grant carries drive.file write (it does not in v1: drive.readonly), so v1 STAGES the cleanup list to michael_staged_items kind 'tasks_cleanup' with the file ids and records counts.cleanup_staged; the Apps Script consumer is out of scope.

Acceptance:
- tasks-classifier.test.js: stale file yields skipped/stale with no Todoist call; unconsumed cleanup yields skipped/cleanup_pending; four-bucket routing from rule fixtures; unrouted items staged; dedupe against a seeded recent task creates nothing; created tasks carry both labels; the cleanup list is staged, never written to Drive in v1

## Architecture
A shared harness (window gate, dedupe, single-flight, ordering, run-row writer) hosts seven small feeders in two venues. Host feeders authenticate once through child C's getAuthenticatedClient and talk to Calendar, Gmail (metadata reads, bounded modify) and Drive through import-time-pure clients. The GHA feeder talks only to Todoist with the existing token. The seat closes the queue the feeders leave (class null, effort_grade null) through a provenance-checked recorder that writes metering. Child E consumes the harness's ordering predicate for assembly; child G consumes the run rows for gauges.

Data flow: 03:45 tasks-classifier (host): Drive current-tasks.json -> rules buckets -> Todoist create / staged items -> feeder_runs. 04:00 calendar-read (host): events.list x2 -> michael_calendar_day -> classification in counts. 04:30 gmail-triage (host): labels.list -> michael_gmail_labels; threads.list -> getThreadMeta -> rules -> michael_gmail_triage_items (intent) -> modifyThread -> action_taken_at, ceiling-bounded; unmatched class null. 04:45 todoist-brief (gha): getTasks -> filter -> grade Est -> michael_todoist_snapshot; auto_apply rules -> mutations_applied. Seat tick (04:30-07:30): queue-read -> Sonnet/Opus sub-agents at the seat -> runner-produced verdict file -> classify-apply -> item/task rows + seat feeder_runs with metering. 05:15+ child E assemble reads assembleReadiness over feeder_runs.

- Overlapping host fires collide on the run-row unique index (MEDIUM/MEDIUM): Single-flight on a running row younger than 10 minutes plus attempt max+1 with a 23505 retry; rollback: A collided fire ends failed and the next */15 fire retries; no data is lost

- Eight PRs each waiting ~13 minutes on the unit tier (HIGH/LOW): Stack independent PRs and merge in dependency order; keep each under 400 LOC; rollback: Any single PR reverts cleanly; the harness is the only shared dependency
